dm_nfr_object.label: Financial Management Systems Modernization
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every posted transaction should originate in a system that is in the audited inventory and posts to the USSGL.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: System inventory, USSGL posting logic per system, transaction volume by system.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: No published execution file names the system a transaction came from. File A, File B and File C carry Treasury accounting elements, not source-system identifiers.

dm_nfr_object.label: Configuration Management
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every production change should have an approved, tested request that predates it.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Change request records, migration logs, production deployment timestamps.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: IT general control evidence is internal to the systems and appears in no published financial file.

dm_nfr_object.label: Security Management
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: A financially relevant system should carry no vulnerability past its remediation date.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: System inventory flagged for financial relevance, vulnerability register with dates.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: Not carried in any published financial file.

dm_nfr_object.label: Access Controls
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every user with access to a financial system should have a current, approved need, and every separation should close every account within the policy window.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Personnel separation records, per-system user listings, provisioning approvals.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: Identity and access data are internal. No published execution file names who recorded a transaction.

dm_nfr_object.label: Segregation of Duties
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: No user should hold both sides of an initiate-and-approve pair; where one does, a documented compensating review should exist for every transaction they touched.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Role-to-capability mapping, user-to-role assignment, transaction-level actor and approver.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: No published file carries an actor or approver on a transaction.

dm_nfr_object.label: Interface Controls
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every record that leaves a feeder system should arrive in the ledger exactly once, at the same value, in the same period.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Record counts and control totals on both sides of each interface, keyed on a shared transaction identifier.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: This site cannot see an internal interface, but it measures the same failure shape between two published files: File A and File B are two reports of the same obligations and disagree in FY2022 and FY2026 (control TIE-01, deliberately non-blocking because the disagreement is real). And File C, the one file that joins an award to an account, holds no row at all for 95 of 171 accounts covering $430.3B. Those are interface losses in the published chain, not inside a Component system.

dm_nfr_object.label: Universe of Transactions
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: The sum of the transaction detail should equal the reported balance, for every balance, on demand.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Transaction-level detail keyed to the reported balance, with a reconciliation to it.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: This site measures a completeness ratio of exactly this shape and publishes it on /linkage: the share of obligations that can be traced from account to award through File C falls from 18.2% in FY2021 to 3.1% in FY2025. That is linkage completeness in the published files, not an error estimate - a dollar absent from File C is not a dollar that was not obligated.

dm_nfr_object.label: Fund Balance with Treasury
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: For each Treasury Account Symbol and month, the Component’s recorded fund balance should equal Treasury’s, and every difference should resolve to a named transaction.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Treasury CARS/GTAS records and Component FBwT detail, keyed on TAS and period.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: File A carries Treasury account symbols and budgetary amounts but no fund-balance position and nothing from the Treasury side, so neither half of the reconciliation is present.

dm_nfr_object.label: Inventory and Stockpile Materials
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every item on the floor should be in the record at a cost traceable to what was paid for it.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Accountable property records, count results, acquisition cost documents.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: This site holds budgetary execution, not proprietary balances. No published file here carries an inventory quantity or an item cost.

dm_nfr_object.label: Operating Materials and Supplies
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Materiel on hand should equal the record, and materiel consumed should have left the record in the period it was consumed.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Accountable records by custody point, count results, consumption postings.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: Proprietary balance; not carried in the execution files on this site.

dm_nfr_object.label: General Property, Plant, and Equipment
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every capitalised asset should trace to a contract and a disbursement that establishes its cost and its in-service date.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Accountable property records, acquisition contracts, disbursement records, in-service dates.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: FPDS on this site carries contract actions from FY2008 onward, which does not reach the acquisition of assets still on the books from earlier decades, and it carries no asset identifier to join on.

dm_nfr_object.label: Real Property
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every structure on an installation should appear once in the financial record at a supportable cost.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Real property inventory, installation records, construction and improvement cost.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: Military construction appears on this site only as budget authority in the -1 exhibits and obligations in File A, never as an asset record.

dm_nfr_object.label: Government Property in the Possession of Contractors
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every contract with a property clause should have a current contractor property report, and those reports should reconcile to the recorded balance.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Contracts carrying property clauses, contractor property reports, the Department’s property record.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: FPDS on this site identifies contract actions and their values but carries no property clause indicator and no property report, so it can bound which contracts might carry the obligation and nothing further. That bound is a starting population, not a test.

dm_nfr_object.label: Joint Strike Fighter Program
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every asset acquired under the programme should be in a Department record that reconciles to the contractor’s.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Programme property records, contractor property reports, contract line detail.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: This site already follows this programme as far as the public chain goes, on /program and /traceability: P-1 line 0147 names the system, account 017-1506 carries $11.93B of obligations in File A, File B adds object class and activity, and File C - the only file that joins an award to an account - holds zero rows for this account. The chain breaks one step before the contract, which is one step before the property.

dm_nfr_object.label: Accounts Payable
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every valid receipt should have a corresponding accounts payable treatment within a defined window, and every payable should trace to a receipt.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Receiving and acceptance transactions, accounts payable subledger, disbursement records, all keyed on a shared transaction identifier.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: No published file on this site carries either side. The nearest public analogue is the obligation-to-award link in File C, which is one relationship upstream and is itself only 3.1% complete in FY2025. Naming the relationship is still worth doing: it is the data requirement a remediation system would have to be built against, and it is the reason an "AP anomaly detector" trained on the payable side alone would be detecting anomalies in the half of the relationship that is present.

dm_nfr_object.label: Environmental and Disposal Liabilities
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every site or asset with a cleanup obligation should be in the inventory the estimate is computed over.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Site and asset inventory, cost estimation model and inputs.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: Environmental restoration appears on this site as appropriation and obligation, never as a liability estimate.

dm_nfr_object.label: Leases
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every arrangement conveying the right to control an asset for a period should be assessed and, where it qualifies, recognised.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Contracts, real property agreements, inter-service support agreements.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: FPDS on this site carries contract actions but no lease classification and no arrangement terms.

dm_nfr_object.label: Unsupported Accounting Adjustments
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every journal entry should trace to a transaction or an approved, evidenced accounting judgement.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Journal entry population with preparer, approver, support reference, and the balance affected.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: No published file carries journal entries.

dm_nfr_object.label: Intragovernmental Transactions and Intradepartmental Eliminations
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Each side of an intragovernmental transaction should record the same amount against the other as trading partner, in the same period.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Transactions carrying a trading partner identifier on both sides, keyed on a shared agreement identifier.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: Trading partner is one of the Standard Line of Accounting elements that does not reach the published files. Of 26 SLOA elements catalogued on /linkage, 9 reach the published files and none reach FPDS.

dm_nfr_object.label: Gross Costs
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Reported cost should accumulate from transactions assigned to a responsibility segment on a documented basis.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Transaction-level cost postings with segment assignment.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: This site holds budgetary execution - obligations and outlays - which is the wrong basis for this assertion, as the root cause says.

dm_nfr_object.label: Earned Revenue
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Revenue recognised in a period should match performance under an agreement in that period.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Reimbursable agreements, performance records, revenue postings.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: File A on this site carries spending authority from offsetting collections at account level, which bounds the reimbursable population by account and by year and reaches nothing at agreement level. Execution on this site defaults to direct activity because File A carries no direct/reimbursable split.

dm_nfr_object.label: Reconciliation of Net Cost of Operations to Outlays
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: One transaction should post both its proprietary and its budgetary entry, so the reconciliation is an identity rather than a calculation.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Transaction-level postings carrying both proprietary and budgetary USSGL accounts.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: File A on this site carries obligations and gross outlays for the same accounts and years, which is the outer shape of the articulation and nothing inside it. Control SBR-03 tests that gross outlays do not exceed total budgetary resources. Note that outlays include payment against prior-year obligations, so the two are not a within-year pair.

dm_nfr_object.label: Budgetary Resources
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every recorded obligation should trace to a document that created it, in the period and the account that document names.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Obligation postings keyed to the obligating document, and the document population itself.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: This is the one weakness on the roster whose assertion the sources here already test. File A is the Statement of Budgetary Resources at account level, and three controls run against it in the load transaction: SBR-01 (obligations plus unobligated balance equals total budgetary resources, within 0.1%), SBR-02 (the resource components foot) and SBR-03 (gross outlays do not exceed total resources). What they test is internal consistency of the published extract, not agreement with the audited statement, and File A carries no obligating document, so the root cause above stays out of reach.

dm_nfr_object.label: Service Organizations
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every complementary user entity control named in a provider’s report should be performed and evidenced by each user Component.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: Provider examination reports, the complementary control inventory, and user Component performance evidence.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: Control-environment evidence; not carried in any published financial file.

dm_nfr_object.label: Component Entity-Level Controls
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: Every process that produces a reported balance should be in the Component’s risk assessment and control documentation.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: A-123 risk assessments, control documentation, monitoring results.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: Control-environment evidence; not carried in any published financial file.

dm_nfr_object.label: DoD-Wide Oversight and Monitoring
dm_nfr_object.expected_relationship: A finding should close only when the control it concerns is shown to operate, in a period after the remediation.
dm_nfr_object.data_required: NFR population with status history, corrective action milestones, and control performance evidence after closure.
dm_nfr_object.coverage_note: This site holds the published counts on this page and nothing at notice level, which is the whole of the problem: closure cannot be distinguished from downgrade or from reissue under a new number without the notice population, and that population is not public.
